_comment: Servable models. Paths are relative to the repo root. Add an entry here to
serve a new checkpoint; no server code changes needed as long as its 'kind'
Every entry MUST name the vocab file its checkpoint was trained against.
Token ids carry no meaning on their own, and two vocabs can share a size while
disagreeing on every pattern -- backends.py cross-checks vocab size against the
checkpoint's lm_head, which catches swapped files but NOT a same-size mismatch.
'd_model'/'layers'/'nhead'/'dim_feedforward' must match how the run was trained
(ARTrainConfig defaults: 256/6/8/1024) or load_state_dict will reject the weights.
An entry with a 'models' list is a GROUP: it shows as one row in /model and
'/model agentic list' asks the server for the members. Set strict_models=false
to let any model name through instead of just the curated list.
Group members are bare model names; the vendor is inferred from the name
(gpt-* -> openai, gemini* -> gemini, claude* -> anthropic). Write
'<vendor>:<model>' explicitly for anything that does not match.

native_oriented.description: 3D-BPE piece AR, native 32^3, ORIENTED. Generates block orientation -- stairs face different ways, logs sit on different axes. Improved successor to native_bpe.
native_oriented.notes: Trained by: python -m blockgen.experiments_native (oriented arm, run_20260721_013119). Its ClusterVocab has oriented=true, so the decoder maps legacy facing/axis data bits into modern blockstate facing=/axis=/type= properties.

native_bpe.description: 3D-BPE piece AR, native 32^3 (T18 arm B). Big builds, chunky streaming.
native_bpe.notes: Trained by: python -m blockgen.experiments_native --epochs 60 (arm B). Vocab was not saved by that run; recovered via scripts/rebuild_native_vocab.py.

canon16_flat.description: Per-voxel AR on canon-16 miniatures (T18 arm A). Highest validity; one block per token.
canon16_flat.notes: Same run as native_bpe (arm A). Miniature regime: 16^3 downsampled, so builds are small. NOTE: run_20260715_062404_native is a --quick 2-epoch smoke of the same arms -- its checkpoint is byte-compatible (identical shapes) but undertrained, so a vocab/lm_head check cannot tell them apart. Use this run.

text_cond.description: CLIP-text-conditioned piece AR (T15). Use /gen <text>; bare /gen samples its null branch.
text_cond.notes: Conditioning fidelity is still weak -- palette transfers, geometry mostly does not. Expect a house, not your house.

agentic.description: Track E: a frontier LLM writes a WorldEdit-style build PROGRAM, executed one command at a time. Real text conditioning -- use /gen <anything>.
agentic.notes: No checkpoint and no training: this is an API model plus blockgen/agentic. Costs money per build (reported in the done message). One in-context example + one repair round by default; see docs/agentic.md for the loop knobs, which are set per entry here.

agentic_plus.description: Agentic with the full loop: plan, one example, two repair rounds and a VISUAL self-critique. Slower and ~4x the cost; use it for the good demo.
agentic_plus.notes: Same group mechanism as 'agentic' -- agentic_plus:<model> works too. The critique round renders the build and shows it back to the model, so the server needs the textured renderer (EGL) available; without it that round is skipped and logged.
